You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

                q=deque([(r,c)]); seen[r][c]=True; cs=[]; col=None

                    rr,cc=q.popleft(); cs.append((rr,cc)); col=gi[rr][cc]
                    for dr,dc in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                        nr,nc=rr+dr,cc+dc
                        if 0<=nr<H and 0<=nc<W and not seen[nr][nc] and gi[nr][nc]!=bg:

                out.append((cs,col,len(cs)))

    print('  changed per row:')
    for r in range(H):
        dots=['' if k else 'X' for k in changed[r]]
        dots=['*' for _ in range(len(dots))]
        print(r, ''.join(dots))

# Re-derive cleanly. G loaded fresh. Analyze pairs 1..2 properly with the right seed color and diff data.
def analyze(i):
    g=G[f'Demo pair {i} input']; o=G[f'Demo pair {i} output']
    cnt={}
    for r in g:
        for x in r: cnt[x]=cnt.get(x,0)+1
    bg=max(cnt,key=lambda k:cnt[k])
    diffs=[(r,c,g[r][c],o[r][c]) for r in range(len(g)) for c in range(len(g[0])) if g[r][c]!=o[r][c]]
    seeds=set((r,c,a) for r,c,a,b in diffs if b==4)
    print('===',i,'bg',bg,'seedcolor counts will be shown')
    from collections import Counter
    cols=Counter(a for _,_,a,_ in diffs)
    # fill = cells whose new value equals some non-bg comp color that is NOT a seed's original color... simplify: show all changed cells grouped by (newval)
    vals=Counter(b for _,_,_,b in diffs)
    print('  diff->newcounts',dict(vals))
    for (r,c,a) in sorted(seeds):
        fills=[(rr,cc,o[rr][cc]) for rr,cc,x,y in diffs if (rr,cc)!=(r,c)]
        ww=[]
        for dr,dx,name in ((-1,0,'U'),(1,0,'D'),(0,-1,'L'),(0,1,'R')):
            nr,nc=r+dr,c+dx; hit=False; dist=0
            while 0<=nr<len(g) and 0<=nc<len(g[0]):
                dist+=1
                if g[nr][nc]!=bg: hit=True; break
                nr+=dr; nc+=dx
            ww.append((name,hit,dist))
        print(f'  seed({r},{c}) origcol{a}: nearest-wall dirs={ww}; filled cells sample={(fills[:6])}')
for i in [1,2]: analyze(i)

Also demo8 (21,24) painted two dirs - maybe because nearest wall distances tie? Test: for each dot compute dir->distance to first non-bg cell; choose dir maximizing distance; if tie, take... examine.
def dir_to_wall(g,r,c,bg):
    H,W=len(g),len(g[0])
    sc={}
    for dy,dx in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
        y,x=r+dy,c+dx;d=0; found=False
        while 0<=y<H and 0<=x<W:
            d+=1
            if g[y][x]!=bg: found=True;break
            if d>=H or d>=W: break
            y+=dy;x+=dx
        if found: sc[(dy,dx)]=d
    return sc
for i in range(1,9):
    g=G[f'Demo pair {i} input']; o=G[f'Demo pair {i} output']
    cnt=Counter(x for r in g for x in r); bg=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    print(f'--- pair{i} bg={bg}')
    for comp in comps(g,bg):
        if len(comp)>1: continue
        (r,c)=comp[0]; v=g[r][c]
        s=dir_to_wall(g,r,c,bg)
        # verify actual output run lengths vs predicted best dir
        best=max(s.items(), key=lambda x:x[1])
        dy,dx=best[0]
        print(' dot',(r,c),'v',v,'walls:',s,'pred-best-dir',(dy,dx))

def f_fix(gi, stop='first', dirs=None):
    h,w=len(gi),len(gi[0]); bg,iso=base(gi)
    out=[r[:] for r in gi]
    D=dirs if dirs else ((0,1),(0,-1),(1,0),(-1,0))
    for y,x,v in iso:
        s=set()
        for dy,dx in D:
            yy,yx=y+dy,x+dx
            while 0<=yy<h and 0<=yx<w and gi[yy][yx]==bg:
                out[yy][yx]=v; s.add((yy,yx))
                yy+=dy; yx+=dx
        out[y][x]=4
        if stop=='first': break
    return out
for stop in ('first',):

        if pr==go: okc+=1
        print(i,'ok:',pr==go)
    print(stop,okc)
